subject: Implement monitor_delegation DBOS workflow
description:
In `capo/workflows/delegation.py`, implement `monitor_delegation` as a `@DBOS.workflow()` with `delegation_id` as the deterministic input. Workflow body: register the per-delegation reader as a `@DBOS.step` (so its progress is checkpointed), poll subprocess `returncode` periodically, transition status on completion to `completed` / `failed` / `killed`.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

_Functional:_
- [ ] `@DBOS.workflow()` with `delegation_id` as deterministic input.
- [ ] Continuous output drain step persists chunks via the batched-insert buffer.
- [ ] Returncode polling at a configurable interval (default 1s).
- [ ] Status transitions: running → completed (returncode 0), failed (non-zero or exception), killed (SIGTERM/SIGKILL signaled by user).
- [ ] All `@DBOS.step` calls with external side effects use the idempotency framework.

_Edge Cases:_
- [ ] Subprocess crashes between two polling cycles: transition to `failed` with reason from stderr/exit code.
- [ ] Workflow re-entered while subprocess is still running: do NOT re-spawn; check existing PID first (per the no-re-attach-by-PID rule, this means the resume path covers spawn).

_Error Handling:_
- [ ] Workflow exception surfaced via Logfire span and reflected on the row as `failed`.

_Performance:_
- [ ] Subprocess output ingest: zero loss + zero pipe blocking on ≥10 MB stdout (re-verifies §6.1 within DBOS context).

**Testing Requirements:**
• Integration: full workflow lifecycle (spawn → drain → completion → status)
• Integration: stress with chatty subprocess
• Integration: kill via signal → status `killed`

Source: internal/specs/capo-SPEC.md Sections 5.6, 9.3
